tex_content.html:
\begin{claim} \end{claim}[Standard solution neck structure far from the tip persists up to time $\theta _0$] For some $A'_0<\infty $, every $A\geq A'_0$ has the property that the standard flow on $(B(p_0,0,A)\setminus B(p_0,0,A/2))\times [0,\theta _0]$ is close to an evolving cylinder. In particular, its time-$t$ distance from $B(p_0,0,A/2)$ to the complement of $B(p_0,0,A)$ exceeds $A/4$. \end{claim}
Proof

\sketch ↗ prop:standard-flow-asymptotic-cylinder This is the asymptotic-cylinder estimate for the standard flow, uniformly on the compact interval $[0,\theta _0]$.

□
